en.title: Object pronouns
en.summary: Object pronouns stand for the person or thing that receives the action.

paragraphs: An object pronoun replaces a noun that is the object of a verb or of a preposition. English has seven: me, you, him, her, it, us and them. Compare the subject pronouns, which come before the verb: I, you, he, she, it, we and they.

An object pronoun follows the verb or the preposition. Only the forms of the personal pronouns change between subject and object; nouns do not. After the verb, you can use it for a thing, but for a person you must choose him, her or them.

blocks.html:
SubjectObjectExample
ImeHe helped me.
youyouI saw you.
hehimWe know him.
sheherThey asked her.
ititShe bought it.
weusHe told us.
theythemI like them.

paragraphs: Some verbs take two objects: the person who receives and the thing that is given. With a pronoun for the person, the order is verb + person + thing, or verb + thing + to + person.

blocks.html:
PatternExample
verb + person + thingShe gave him the book.
verb + thing + to + personShe gave the book to him.
both pronounsShe gave it to him. (not: She gave him it, in most dialects)

items: Wrong: **Me and him went home.** Right: **He and I went home.** (subject forms are used for the subject)
Wrong: **This is between you and I.** Right: **This is between you and me.** (after a preposition use the object form)
Wrong: **Give to me it.** Right: **Give it to me.**
Use object forms after verbs and prepositions.
Keep I for the subject; use me after a preposition: with me, for me.
After than and as, careful speech uses the subject form with an understood verb: She is taller than I (am). In informal speech, than me is common.
